body.statement: Determine whether \(\textsc{Explicit-Max-Tail}\), parameterized by \(k\), admits an \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n,L,\ell)\) exact algorithm or is \(\mathrm{W}[1]\)-hard. Separately determine whether either conclusion survives when the input support is uniform and generated by a fixed-dimensional balance rule; no such hardness is asserted here.
body.justification: The theorem-level XP and NP-completeness results leave the genuine parameterized boundary unresolved.
body.gap: Neither exact rank computation nor missing-data testing currently classifies this parameter, and the weighted reduction does not answer the uniform balance-generated case.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether large trials with a modest number of missing endpoints need approximation or can have fixed-parameter exact inference.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether the exact problem parameterized by the number \(k\) of missing outcomes is \(\mathrm{FPT}\) or is \(\mathrm{W}[1]\)-hard, and whether either classification persists for a uniform support generated by a fixed-dimensional balance rule.
obligation.obstruction: The chamber enumeration has an exponent depending on \(k\), while the weighted \(\textsc{Clique}\) reduction maps the target parameter to the graph order rather than to the clique size. Its unequal guard and vertex weights also cannot be replaced by duplicate support rows because the support is a set, so it does not establish the uniform generated-support case.
obligation.attempted: Dynamic programming over support-column types leaves a vector of rowwise rank-sum comparisons whose dimension grows with the explicitly listed support. The lowest-tied-block reduction was also examined for parameter-preserving uniformization, but distinct fixed-count gadget rows that reproduce the unequal weights without changing the converse were not obtained.
obligation.partial_result: The proved upper bound is the exact \(\mathrm{XP}\) running time \(O((2n+1)^k nL\operatorname{poly}(\ell))\), including an \(O(nL\operatorname{poly}(\ell))\) sweep when \(k=1\).  The proved lower bound is NP-completeness when \(k\) is part of the input.  The reduction has target parameter \(k=v=|V|\), rather than a function only of the source clique size \(s\), and therefore is not a parameterized reduction establishing \(\mathrm{W}[1]\)-hardness.  No conclusion has been proved for uniform supports generated by a fixed-dimensional balance rule.
